A face serum is a light, concentrated step that sits between cleansing and moisturising. Most are watery or gel-like and carry one or two key ingredients, such as vitamin C, hyaluronic acid or niacinamide. Here is what each of those ingredients is, how to choose a serum, and how to layer it.

Serum, moisturiser or face oil?

  • Water-based serums are thin and quick to absorb. They go on first, after cleansing and toning.
  • Moisturisers are creams or lotions that hold moisture in. They go on after your serum.
  • Oil serums are blends of plant oils. They can be used last at night, or mixed with a drop of moisturiser.

Vitamin C serum

Vitamin C is an antioxidant, and one of the most searched serum ingredients. Pure vitamin C (ascorbic acid) can be unstable, so many serums use a gentler, more stable form. Deyga 10% Vitamin C Face Serum (from £16.99, 20ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with orange and citrus extracts. Use a vitamin C serum in the morning, and always finish with sunscreen. See every vitamin C serum.

Hyaluronic acid serum

Hyaluronic acid is a moisture-loving ingredient that holds water in the skin, so it suits every skin type, including oily skin. Deyga 2% Hyaluronic Acid Serum (£22.99, 20ml) combines sodium hyaluronate with glycerine, panthenol, aloe vera and centella asiatica, and is made without fragrance. Vilvah Milk Drops Hydrating Serum (from £21.99) pairs aloe vera juice and hyaluronic acid with rice milk extract and alpha arbutin. Apply either to slightly damp skin.

Niacinamide, bakuchiol and ceramides

Niacinamide is a form of vitamin B3 that is easy to pair with other ingredients. If you are looking for a niacinamide serum, read the full ingredient list: niacinamide often works alongside other ingredients rather than on its own. Bakuchiol is a plant extract often used as a gentle alternative to retinol, and ceramides are lipids that are naturally found in skin. Vilvah Better Ageing Serum (£28.99, 20ml) brings all three together, with hyaluronic acid, olive squalane, blue pea flower extract and a plant peptide extract. The Vilvah AM PM Serum Kit (£47.99) pairs it with Milk Drops: Milk Drops in the morning, Better Ageing at night. For dry, mature skin, Highborn London MOISTUREBURST Serum (from £57) is a ceramide serum made to layer under moisturiser.

Face oil serums

Oil serums suit dry skin and evening routines. Deyga Rose Glow Serum (£17.99, 30ml) blends rose and saffron with coconut, pomegranate seed, rosehip, almond and jojoba oils. Deyga Beautifying Serum (from £17.99, 30ml) uses moringa, kukui, grapeseed and vetiver oils. Warm two or three drops between your palms and press them into the skin.

How to choose a face serum

  • Dry or tight skin: hyaluronic acid, ceramides or a face oil at night.
  • Oily skin: a light hyaluronic acid serum, which can be enough on its own on warm days.
  • Dull-looking skin: a vitamin C serum in the morning, with sunscreen.
  • Sensitive skin: a short, fragrance-free list, and one new product at a time.

How to layer a serum

  1. Cleanse with a face wash that suits you: see face wash for your skin type.
  2. Apply 2 or 3 drops of a water-based serum to slightly damp skin and press it in.
  3. Go thinnest to thickest: serum, then eye cream, then moisturiser. Read moisturiser for your skin type and our under eye cream guide.
  4. In the morning, finish with SPF. Browse every sunscreen.

You do not need several serums. One in the morning and one at night is plenty for most people.

Good to know

  • Patch test a new serum on your jaw or inner arm for 24 hours.
  • Introduce one new serum at a time, so you know what suits your skin.
  • Store serums with the cap closed, away from heat and sunlight, and use them within the time shown on the pack.
  • Stinging, redness or itching that lasts is worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

Shop every serum, explore hydration and glow, or the full skincare range, all dispatched from the UK.

A good moisturiser is the step that holds the rest of your routine together. It softens skin, helps it feel comfortable all day and gives make-up or sunscreen a smooth base. But the right texture depends on your skin: a rich cream that rescues dry skin can feel heavy on oily skin, and a light lotion may not be enough in winter. Here is how to choose a moisturiser for your skin type.

Cream, lotion or gel: what is the difference?

Most moisturisers mix water with oils and butters. The more oil and butter, the richer the texture:

  • Rich creams hold more butters and oils, such as shea butter and almond oil. They suit dry and very dry skin, and cold weather.
  • Light creams and lotions have more water and lighter oils. They suit normal, oily and combination skin.
  • Gels and serums are mostly water with moisture-loving ingredients such as glycerine and hyaluronic acid. They work on their own for oily skin, or under a cream.

Moisturiser for dry skin

Dry skin feels tight, may flake and drinks a light lotion straight in. Look for a cream with butters and oils.

Deyga Deep Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) blends shea butter with marula and almond oils, centella asiatica (gotu kola) and cardamom, and Deyga makes it without artificial fragrance. Highborn London Imperial Moisturiser (£46, 50ml) is a richer, nourishing cream made in England for dry, tight-feeling skin. See more moisturisers for dry skin.

Moisturiser for oily skin

Oily skin still needs moisture: skipping it can leave skin feeling tight while it still looks shiny. Choose a light, fast-absorbing texture.

Deyga Light Moisturising Face Cream (£18.99, 30g) is made for oily and normal skin, with rosehip, almond and avocado oils, shea butter, centella asiatica and ectoin, and a hint of vanilla essential oil. A good cleanse is the first step of every skincare routine, and the wrong face wash can undo the rest. Too harsh, and skin feels tight and dry; too rich, and oily skin feels heavy. Here is how to choose a face wash for your skin type, what the different textures and ingredients mean, and how to cleanse.

First, know your skin type

Wash with a mild cleanser, pat dry and wait about an hour without applying anything. Then look and feel:

  • Dry: feels tight, and may look flaky or dull.
  • Oily: looks shiny all over, especially on the forehead, nose and chin.
  • Combination: shiny in the centre, normal or dry on the cheeks.
  • Sensitive: easily stings, turns red or reacts to fragrance.

Face wash for dry skin

Dry skin needs a cleanser that lifts away the day without stripping. Look for creamy or milky textures and soothing, moisture-loving ingredients.

Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml) combines oat milk with provitamin B5, kaolin and mild cleansers made from coconut and corn. Deyga makes it for dry, sensitive and normal skin. Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash (£9.99, 100ml) is a soft cream with banana fruit extract, hydrolysed wheat protein and glycerine. Shop every face wash for dry skin.

Face wash for sensitive skin

If your skin reacts easily, keep the ingredient list short and skip added fragrance. The Vilvah Fragrance-Free Cream Face Wash is made without fragrance, and Vilvah describes it as pH-balanced. The Deyga Oat Milk Face Wash is mild too, but it does contain fragrance, so patch test it first. See more for sensitive skin.

Face wash for oily skin

Oily skin likes a foaming or gel wash that leaves skin feeling fresh but not squeaky. Over-washing can make skin feel tighter without making it any less shiny, so twice a day is enough.

  • Vilvah Honey Face Wash (£12.99, 100ml): 10% raw honey with papaya and blackberry extracts, witch hazel and gotu kola, and a citrus-vanilla scent. Vilvah makes it for normal to oily skin, with a medium foam.
  • Vilvah Milk Powder Face Wash (£13.99, 50g): a water-free powder that turns to foam in wet hands, with rice powder, rice milk extract, oat flour, hyaluronic acid and papain, a papaya enzyme. Fragrance-free and made for normal to oily skin.

Shop every face wash for oily skin and more for oily skin.

Tea tree, charcoal and vitamin C face washes

Tea tree and charcoal

Deyga Charcoal Face Wash (from £12.99, 100ml) is a gel built on tea tree hydrosol, with activated charcoal from coconut shell and gentle coconut and corn-based cleansers. It is a popular pick if you are looking for a tea tree face wash: fresh-feeling, and made for all skin types.

Vitamin C

Deyga Vitamin C Foaming Face Wash (£15.99, 100ml) uses ascorbyl glucoside, a stable form of vitamin C, with citron, bitter orange and lemon hydrosols in a light foam. A bright, zesty wash for the morning.

Cream, foam or powder?

  • Cream and milk washes feel the softest: good for dry and sensitive skin.
  • Foams and gels feel fresh and light: good for oily and combination skin. Shiseido Complete Cleansing Microfoam (£29.99, 180ml) is a fine, lightweight foam for everyday use.
  • Powders are mixed with water as you use them, and travel well.
  • A luxury cleanser: Highborn London Crystal Cleanser (£24, 100ml) contains co-enzyme Q10 and is made for morning and night.

How to wash your face

  1. Wet your face with lukewarm water, not hot.
  2. Use a small amount, about the size of a 5p coin, and work it into a lather in your hands.
  3. Massage gently for 30 to 60 seconds, including the hairline and jaw. Keep it away from your eyes.
  4. Rinse well and pat dry with a clean towel.
  5. Follow straight away with toner or moisturiser while skin is still slightly damp.

Most people do best washing twice a day: morning and night. If you wear make-up or sunscreen, cleanse twice at night: once to lift it, once to clean the skin.

After cleansing

A cleanser is only the first step. Add a toner if you like one, then a moisturiser: see our moisturisers for dry skin, or read moisturiser for your skin type. Once or twice a week, add a mask: see our face mask guide. Light, soothing layers such as aloe vera gel suit oily skin; read how to use aloe vera gel. Not sure which natural brand suits you? Compare them in Deyga or Vilvah.

Good to know

  • Patch test any new face wash on your jaw or inner arm first.
  • Change one thing at a time, so you know what suits you.
  • Breakouts, redness or itching that last are worth showing to a pharmacist or your GP.

Browse every cleanser and the full skincare range, all dispatched from the UK.
